newsitem.title: GERMANY: Most Germans want Scientology under observation.
newsitem.headline: Most Germans want Scientology under observation.

text.p: Most Germans want the Church of Scientology placed under observation by the government's anti-extremist watchdog agency, according to a survey released on Wednesday.

The survey, conducted for Bavarian television, found that 59.2 percent of respondents were in favour of calling in the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution to keep a eye on the controversial organisation.
Only 9.5 percent were against the measure while 31.3 percent either had no opinion or did know what Scientology was.
Of those who had heard of the organisation, 40.6 percent favoured banning it altogether, according to the survey of 508 people carried out by the Allensbach polling group.

Germany and the Los Angeles-based church have been engaged in a fierce war of words over the last few months. Scientology has compared Germany's treatment of its members to Nazi persecution of the Jews before World War Two.

Germany does not accord Scientology the status of a religion, believing it to be a purely economic organisation. Officials say it exploits the insecurities of its members to make big profits from expensive self-improvement courses.

Bavaria has been at the forefront of the fight against Scientology, excluding companies run by Scientologists from public tenders and asking applicants for public sector jobs whether they belong to the group.

The conservative southern state has already put Scientolgy under observation by its own regional anti-extremist agency. Officials are currently considering whether the practice should be extended nationwide.
